sections.h2: Why would a Monroe-area seller need the Union County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Because the sale is not complete in the public record until your deed is filed there. The office keeps what its website calls a permanent record of land ownership and transfers for Union County, covering deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, assumed names and powers of attorney.

Birth, death and marriage certificates, marriage licenses, military discharge papers and notary commissions also run through this desk, and it doubles as a passport acceptance facility open to anyone. A house seller cares about the land side only. Whoever handles your closing delivers the signed deed, and the time stamp on it settles who stands first if two claims ever collide.

The department page says the office has served Union County since the county was formed in 1842, and that the register is an elected official. A quick cash sale of a Union County house still ends at this counter.

sections.h2: Can the Union County register tell you what a document means?
sections.html:
No. The department describes itself as a recording office only, and it says North Carolina law forbids the register and staff from practicing law.

Staff will not hand out legal forms, coach you through filling one in, or say what a filed instrument does to your rights. For all of that the department tells visitors to see an attorney. This comes up most with title changes: to add or remove a name from a deed, you record a fresh deed, because the office does not edit an old one.

  • Liens and judgments against a person or property: the Clerk of Court, 704-698-3100.
  • Who owns a given street address: the tax assessor, 704-283-3746, since the register indexes by name.
  • Drafting or correcting a deed: a North Carolina attorney.

sections.h2: How and when do you file a deed in Union County?
sections.html:
Walk it in during recording hours, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., or route it through an electronic recording vendor. The Union County Government Center at 500 North Main Street, Monroe, houses the office, and the department lists neighborhood covenant files on the second floor.

Three vendors are named as currently in use: Simplifile, CSC and ePN. You contact the vendor to get set up, which is why most sellers never touch this step. Title companies and law firms that run closings tend to hold accounts already. Ask yours which vendor they use and when to expect the recorded copy back.

Paper filers need the original signed document plus payment. State law says fees are collected before filing, so an unpaid document will sit.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees and transfer tax in Union County?
sections.html:
The department prints $26.00 for the first fifteen pages and $4.00 per further page when it explains how to record separation papers, and state law uses the same pair of numbers for instruments generally. The excise tax on deeds is $2 per thousand dollars for deeds since August 1, 1991.

Documents that miss the layout rules pick up $25.00 more. Ask the office for its current fee sheet before mailing a check.

sections.h2: Who pays the Union County deed excise tax?
sections.html:
The person giving up the property pays it. The legislature words the rate as one dollar for each $500 of value, which matches the $2 per thousand the county shows, and requires payment to the register before the deed goes on record.

In an ordinary sale that is the seller, and the charge appears as a line on the settlement statement. The collected tax splits evenly between the county general fund and the state, with the county permitted to hold back a small cut of the state half.

The dollar amount turns on the price or value stated in the deed, so get the number from your closing office rather than estimating.

sections.h2: What can you search online in Union County, and what needs a visit?
sections.html:
Online, the register offers deeds from 1973 and maps from 1842. Earlier deeds and every other record type need a trip to the office.

Two limits catch people. The deed look-up covers deeds and plats only, so mortgage information is not there. And the index is built on names, so typing a street address into it gets you nowhere.

  • Know the owner's name as it appears on the last deed.
  • Call the assessor for the owner of a street address.
  • Go to the office for mortgages and deeds of trust.
  • Look in the same office for filed HOA covenants, if the county holds them.

Sellers use the search to check that the signers match the names on title and that no old deed of trust is still open.

sections.h2: Why does the order of recording matter in Union County?
sections.html:
A conveyance, an option, a right of first refusal or a lease over three years binds lien creditors and buyers for value only once registered in the county holding the land. Competing instruments rank by registration time.

That rule is why a delay between signing and recording can matter, and why an uncancelled deed of trust on an inherited or long-held house deserves attention before you sign a sales contract. Lenders do not charge to record a release, since satisfactions carry no fee.

Ask for the recorded copy after closing and keep it with your sale papers.

sections.h2: Which other Union County offices come up in a home sale?
sections.html:
The assessor, the Clerk of Court and the register cover most questions. The assessor's number is 704-283-3746, the Clerk of Court's is 704-698-3100, and the register's vital records line is 704-283-3610 per the department's pages.

Notary commissions are also kept here. A notary who is renewing takes the oath in person for a $10.00 fee. Have your closing office confirm that the notary witnessing your signature holds a current commission.

Probate, divorce and tax questions follow their own paths through the courts and the tax office. The register only files what those processes hand over.

faqs.q: What hours does the Union County Register of Deeds keep?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Electronic filers go through Simplifile, CSC or ePN, so ask your vendor about its cutoff.

faqs.q: Will the Union County register draft my deed?
faqs.a: No. The department calls itself a recording office only, and staff cannot supply legal forms or advise on completing them. Hire an attorney to prepare the deed.

faqs.q: What is the Union County deed excise tax?
faqs.a: The county shows $2 per thousand dollars for deeds from August 1, 1991 on. State law words it as $1.00 per $500 of value, and the seller usually pays at closing.

faqs.q: Can I look up a Union County deed by street address?
faqs.a: Not in the register's index, which runs on names. For an address, call the tax assessor at 704-283-3746. Online deeds start in 1973.

faqs.q: Is there a charge to record a satisfaction in Union County?
faqs.a: State law lists no fee for recording satisfactions or cancellations of deeds of trust or mortgages. Confirm with the office when you file.
